About this map

This interactive map was developed within the framework of the Hubs4Circularity Community of Practice project by Strane Innovation.

Methodology

1) Outgoing flows (waste generation)

The estimation of waste flows at facility level is based on a combination of two complementary European datasets:

  • Eurostat – Generation of waste by waste category, hazardousness and NACE Rev.2 activity
    This dataset provides sector-level distributions of waste types by economic activity.
  • E-PRTR (European Pollutant Release and Transfer Register)
    This database provides facility-level data, including total quantities of waste generated by industrial sites.

The methodology consists of deriving waste composition ratios for each NACE sector using Eurostat data. These ratios represent the relative share of each waste category within a sector.

These sectoral ratios are then applied to the total waste quantities reported at facility level in the E-PRTR database. This allows the reconstruction of a detailed breakdown of waste streams for each individual facility.

This approach enables a consistent and harmonised estimation of waste flows across Europe, while preserving the spatial resolution of the E-PRTR dataset.

2) Incoming flows (material demand proxy)

Incoming flows are not directly available at facility level. They are therefore estimated using a proxy approach based on economic production data.

  • Eurostat COMEXT database
    Provides economic values of goods produced and traded, classified according to the CPA (Classification of Products by Activity) nomenclature and linked to NACE sectors.

From this dataset, sector-specific ratios are calculated, representing the relative importance of each product category (CPA) within a given economic sector.

These ratios are then combined with the total waste generated by each facility (from E-PRTR) to compute an inflow importance indicator.

This indicator does not represent a physical mass flow. Instead, it is a proxy for material demand intensity, based on the assumption that:

facilities generating larger quantities of waste are likely to process larger amounts of raw materials.

By scaling sectoral product ratios with facility-level waste quantities, this method highlights:

  • potential input material needs,
  • relevant resource categories,
  • and spatial hotspots of industrial demand.

This approach is particularly useful for identifying opportunities for industrial symbiosis, even in the absence of direct data on material inputs.

3) SCALER synergy detection

The detection of potential industrial synergies is based on the results of the European project SCALER (scalerproject.eu).

Within this project, a set of 100 high-potential industrial symbiosis solutions was identified, covering a wide range of resource exchanges between industries.

For a subset of these synergies, it was possible to associate:

  • a NACE code for the emitting industry,
  • a NACE code for the receiving (user) industry.

In this tool, synergies are automatically detected by:

  • matching facility NACE codes with emitter profiles,
  • matching other facilities with corresponding user profiles,
  • identifying all possible emitter–user combinations within the study area.

This enables the dynamic identification of:

  • potential industrial partnerships,
  • resource exchange opportunities,
  • and territorial symbiosis networks.

The SCALER module therefore provides a decision-support layer to complement the flow analysis, helping stakeholders move from data visualisation to actionable circular economy strategies.

Disclaimer
This tool provides a modelling-based decision-support visualisation. Results rely on statistical approximations and proxies, and should be interpreted as indicative insights rather than exact physical flows.
